svg.title: Exposio system architecture
svg.desc: Client-side k-anonymity, an ownership gate, stateless edge functions, and no persistence layer.
svg.text: Ownership-verified breach exposure assessment. No database, no accounts, no analytics — every request is answered from a signed token and then discarded.
everything here runs on the person’s own device
k-anonymity · the server never sees it
serverless functions · nothing is kept between one request and the next
issues a one-time code and a signed
returns a scan token, valid 15 minutes
no network, no storage · the same code runs
on the server, in the browser, in the tests
No database. No object store. No accounts.
No record of who asked about what.
The whole of the session lives in a signed token
held by the browser, and expires with it.
Nothing to breach, subpoena, sell or leak later.
1. Enters their email address or phone
Until step 3 completes, no lookup occurs.
The password is hashed on the device, and
only the first 5 characters of that hash are
Exposio never receives it in any form.
checked before the payload is parsed, and the
payload carries a keyed hash of the identifier,
the password path goes straight to Pwned Passwords, over the top of Exposio
Browser → Exposio: the address being checked, and the token proving it was verified. Never the password, in any form.
Exposio → third parties: the address, to the breach sources; the contents of the report, to the language model. Never a stored record, because none exists.
Exposio → disk: nothing at all. The mail and SMS modules log a status code, and never the recipient.
MSc research prototype · Óbuda University · the diagram covers Breach Risk, component B of the Exposure Score
